recipes.name: Slow Cooker Apple Crisp
ingredients_raw: 0.33333334326744 cup white sugar, or to taste
6 cups apples - peeled, cored and chopped

steps.text: To make the topping: Mix flour, brown sugar, white sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt together in a bowl. Add butter and mix with your fingers or a fork until coarse crumbs form. Stir in walnuts.
To make the apple filling: Whisk sugar, cornstarch, ginger, and cinnamon together in a small bowl.

Place apples in a slow cooker. Stir in cornstarch mixture. Add lemon juice and toss to combine. Sprinkle topping over apples. Cover and cook until apples are tender, on Low for 4 hours or High for 2 hours.
Turn off the slow cooker, partially uncover, and let stand until topping has hardened, about 1 hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Apple Crisp
raw_recipe.description: Easy crockpot apple crisp made in the slow cooker with sugar-sweetened apples and a delicious walnut crumb topping flavored with cinnamon and nutmeg.

video.description: Believe it! In this video, you’ll see how to make a 5-star apple crisp in your slow cooker. You’ll simply place chopped apples (a mix of sweet and tart) in the crock pot, stir in a cinnamon-ginger mixture, and top with a walnut crumb. Then cook on High until the apples are tantalizingly tender.

review.reviewBody: First off, (and I mean this in a polite way) for those of you saying there's no sense in doing this in a crock pot when you have the do the work either way with the apples, you are missing the point of having a crock pot in the first place. It frees up your time so that you do not have to keep such a watchful eye on it. My husband had to go work this morning, on a Sunday, and so he just switched on my crock pot for me when he left the house. Everything was already in there...and when I woke up, I had fresh apple crisp, already cooked and just waiting to be eaten. Moving on...this turned out perfectly! I left my apples in slices since they were small apples. I also adjusted this recipe to be gluten free and free of refined sugars. I actually mixed the walnuts in with the apples rather than the topping. And I used xylitol in place of sugar, adding some molasses to the crumb topping to add the richness of brown sugar. I don't care for ginger in my desserts, so I just used cinnamon and nutmeg for the spices. I also used a lot less sweeteners...only about 1/4 cup of xylitol in the apples and 1/3 cup in the crumb topping, with about 1/4 cup of the molasses. I also omitted the cornstarch and just used a few Tbsp. of GF baking mix. I used Earth Balance in place of butter, and it works great. I can tell you the taste is the same, even with my changes. I've made apple crisps the way as printed before going GF. They are both great.

Great recipe! I added 1cup of oats to the topping and it was just right. Cooked on high for 2 hours and then moved the top to crisp up the topping for another hour. I used 7 grannsy smith apples instead of 6 and I almost wish I had used 8 because they really cook down. However the flavor was still amazing! Add some vanilla ice cream and holy wow!

For those of you dreading the apple prep, I used the victorio apple slice/corer/peeler. Whole prep took me 15 minutes.

I read all the reviews. Great comments! 
Changes: I cut down the sugar to a total of a 1/2 cup using brown sugar only....1/4 cup for each, apples and topping. 6 cups of sliced apples called Opal. 1 cup rolled oats.

The MOST IMPORTANT CHANGE that makes the biggest difference is to cover the crock pot with a clean dish towel and then put the lid on. Bake it like that till the time is up without peeking. The dish towel absorbs the condensation. The apple crisp comes out more baked. I live in the south and if I can keep the heat of the oven from running our central ac unit I feel very happy saving the cost of electricity.
Low for 4 hrs seems better than high for 2hrs.

I used Macintosh apples and doubled the recipe. I would say doubling the recipe makes a proper 6 servings. The recipe is absolutley wonderful! I cooked it on high for 3 hours and then opened it up and put it on keep warm for 30 min. I will absolutely be making this recipe again!!!

When I looked in the crock pot after an hour, I was a little worried. But oh my goodness, when it finished. Wow! Best apple crisp I've ever had, and so easy. 

I doubled the recipe and used a 6-quart crock pot. Increased the cooking time from 2 hours to 3 hours before removing the lid. I used 1/2 granny smith and 1/2 gala apples.

I adjusted this for 3 servings and made it in a 4 qt slow cooker. I replaced half the flour with oatmeal and used pecans instead of walnuts because that is what I had. Like another reviewer I cooked 3 hours on low and then rotated the lid 90 degrees to leave both ends of the oval cooker uncovered. As my dad would have said, it was "larrupping"!

I made this for a potluck at work. Everyone raved about it. I didn't have any ginger, so I substituted cardamom. It was wonderful. This is going to be my new go-to dessert recipe. Since my gala apples were small I just sliced them with my apple corer/slicer, and I went through the 3 pounds of apples in no time. I prepared my apples the night before, and left them soaking in a lemon juice water mixture in the refrigerator. I also combined the dry ingredients the night before. Then when I got up in the morning all I had to do was dump everything in the crock pot and go to work. I may cut down on the sugar next time because it was quite sweet, but that's what everybody seemed to like.

This was my first attempt at apple crisp. Instead of chopping the apples I sliced them thin, and stirred in a bit of rolled oats (about 1/4 - 1/3 cup worth) into the topping as someone suggested. It tastes fantastic with vanilla bean ice cream!
Only 4 stars because there's no oats. I added a cup of oats and 1/4 cup butter to compensate. Yum!

Very, very good! Great for a crisp fall day. I too add some quick cooking oats to the topping. Also drizzled butterscotch ice cream topping over the apples before the topping. As someone else suggested, made on low for 3 hours then put the lid sideways across so ends were open for another hour. Topping was nice and crunchy.

Fantastic! I used a mixture of fruits (Granny Smith, peaches and plums) to clean out the fruit drawer and used about half the sugar and it turned out fantastic! My picky eater even enjoyed a little bit of it! We topped it with raspberry white chocolate ice cream!
Easy to make and delicious!
I loved it. The only variation I used was different kinds of 🍏 🍎 Very good mmm 😋
Absolutely my favorite!!!
My husband loved this. I will make this for Thanksgiving instead of apple pie.

when i was making it i was thinking this is alot of dry stuff to go in with just apples for liquid ..i added 1/2 cup water apples then another 1/3 cup to the top after everything was said and done then cooked .. turned out not to bad better than i thought it would ..deffinatly tastes better cold than hot

I made this recipe using McIntosh apples and it turned out yummy. I didn’t use any nutmeg or lemon juice and I added 1/3 cup brown sugar to the apples too. I didn’t have cornstarch, so I used self rising flour instead. I also used self rising flour for the topping. I always make my apple crisp in my crockpot, but have always used the oatmeal topping and granny smith apples, but I forgot the oatmeal, so I used this recipe instead. I got theses apples because they were on sale. I also used dark brown sugar instead of light brown.
Yummy and so easy
Absolutely delicious!! Thank you for this great recipe. I can even make it with sugar substitute.!
I thought it was good, and I like using my crock pot when I get a chance. Definitely serve with vanilla ice cream- it's a wonderful combo.
